items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: He gave Chuck Mangione one, he gave Pat one, he gave me one.

ctx.x: Well I wondered how you, like if there was a real door that opened you, for your composing and I think you said Buddy Rich because you came back and started writing for him, is that correct?

Yes. I enjoyed the band. You know he respected me and if he respected you he would take a chance on you — if he respected you as a player he’d take a chance on you as a writer. That’s why a lot of the guys in the band were writing charts for the band, because he respected their playing and he would listen to what they had to write. Well I was on the Glenn Miller band for three years, almost three years with Buddy DeFranco. And I learned a lot from him as well. So all the time I was on the Glenn Miller band I was…

it to your apartment, because you know it’s not worth anything, it’s just like a used car, they’ll give you so much for the trade in. Anyway, long story short, I was on unemployment and I heard that Buddy had signed, Pat told me that Buddy had signed with RCA Victor. And so I was making fifty bucks a week on unemployment and then doing odd jobs. A bus trip to Philadelphia was 25 bucks. So I bought a bus ticket to Philadelphia with this “Piece of the Road” suite that I wrote. And everybody was there at the club,…

items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Joel had been working with my brother in ... Gap Mangione’s band, and he had worked with Chuck Mangione and my brother Joe. And so I knew that he could play the gig.

ctx.x: Did you ever let a guy go that Buddy disagreed with? Like why did you let him go?

I let guys go — I had to fire guys who basically, yeah guys he disagreed with also, but also there were guys that weren’t up to the level yet and had to go. I mean I’m not going to name names but there were guys that we had to do that. It was just part of the thing. And once he got somebody that he liked, Joel DeBartolo was really I think one of the ones that stayed for quite a bit and that was a kind of a story, I don’t know how much time you’ve got with that. But you know Joel had been working with my brother…

Rochester, with Gap Mangione’s band, and he had worked with Chuck Mangione and my brother Joe. And so I knew that he could play the gig. I hired him on the gig, he comes, and we were playing in St. Louis, Missouri in a big hotel, and Joel had never seen the book. Now Joel was kind of nervous, he was very nervous, and Joel had a stutter. He really had a problem stuttering. He ended up playing in the Tonight Show band with Johnny Carson for years. You know he was the bass player. So I got Joel on and Joel came on…
